A student wishing to withdraw from a course must petition, in concert with his/her adviser, the appropriate Student Review and Promotion Committee.  This committee will make recommendations to the Dean for a final decision.  Upon discretion of the appropriate student Review and Promotion Committee, consideration of withdrawal from a course, clerkship or other learning experience may be recommended to the student, his/her adviser and the Dean.  A student may not leave school prior to completion of an academic year unless granted leave of absence by the Dean for Student Affairs.  A student who leaves without such permission or who fails to return by the end of his/her granted term of leave, is considered terminated from his/her class. medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The mission of the ECU BSOM Office of Student Success and Wellness is to deliver personalized, proactive, and holistic support that empowers and inspires each learner to reach academic, personal, and professional goals and to flourish at BSOM and beyond. The office provides academic counseling and coaching services as well as wellness support to assist medical students in the foundational science and clinical phases of medical school with a variety of concerns. Transition to medical school, study skill/exam preparation support, USMLE Step 1 and USMLE Step 2 CK preparation, clerkship support, maintaining self-care while meeting the demands of medical school, and career support to help students clarify career concerns are among the common medical student concerns that office staff work to assist students with. Confidential mental health counseling services are also provided to students through the office by an onsite licensed mental health clinician to help students navigate through personal challenges, enhance personal growth and mental wellbeing, and strengthen resiliency skills.

medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The BSOM curriculum is designed to offer early immersion in a variety of clinical settings while laying the foundation of knowledge for the practice of medicine. Your education is delivered in a spiral architecture with planned, spaced repetition that ensures you return to key concepts over time with increasing complexity.

The 20-month Foundational Phase consists of the traditional basic sciences content embedded within courses that begin to develop your clinical skills, critical thinking, and understanding of social and systemic forces in health systems. This phase contains an immersion in clinical care experiences including a longitudinal primary and community care preceptorship. Activities focused on professional identity formation, wellness, lifelong learning skills, and reflection are woven throughout the Foundations of Doctoring course.

The Clinical Phase is 12 months and includes six Core Clerkships and 4 weeks of elective time devoted to career exploration. The Radiology Clerkship is a longitudinal experience integrated and aligned with each of the Core Clerkships.

The Differentiation Phase spans the final 13 months of the curriculum and includes the required Advanced Core Clerkships and ample elective time to allow students to further explore their career interests and individualize their learning experiences.

An innovative Health Systems Science curriculum is longitudinally interwoven throughout the four-year curriculum to prepare students to care for patients, families, and communities in a rapidly changing healthcare environment.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: In 1972, East Carolina University enrolled students in the First-Year Program in Medical Education. The Board of Governors and the State General Assembly authorized the expansion to a degree-granting School of Medicine in 1975, and the first class was enrolled in August 1977. The school's educational facilities are located in the nine-story Brody Medical Sciences Building on the 100-acre Health Sciences Center campus.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The Brody School of Medicine’s mission is to increase the supply of primary care physicians serving Eastern North Carolina and the state, to improve the health and well-being of the region, and to train physicians who will meet the health care needs of the state.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
https://medicine.ecu.edu/admissions/application-process/

We conduct a complete and holistic review of applications, and encourage students to submit them as early in the cycle as possible. Following an initial review, many students will receive a secondary application. Students are expected to return their secondary applications by the deadline.

Legal residents of North Carolina are considered for admission. Graduates from the UNC System public schools within 5 years of application submission are eligible for consideration, regardless of state of residence. A bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited regional institution within the US or Canada is required for admissions. We do not accept international applicants.

medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We understand and appreciate the diverse educational pathways that individuals may pursue on their journey towards a career in medicine. Courses taken at the community college level completed during high school and/or a two-year transfer program will satisfy our prerequisites. However, the Admissions Committee does prefer that the bulk of the courses, particularly Biology, Chemistry, and Biochemistry courses, be taken at a four-year college or university. For college graduates seeking prerequisite course completion post graduation, we encourage completing prerequisite courses at a 4-year institution or pursuing graduate level science coursework. Courses take for AP credit and online courses cannot be used to meet prerequisite requirements.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: We do not accept letters of intent, updates, or additional changes post application submission. The only new information that will be considered are new MCAT scores and required letters of recommendation, both of which are submitted to AMCAS.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Medical education at the Brody School of Medicine (BSOM) requires the acquisition of a broad base of scientific knowledge alongside the development of essential skills and professional behaviors. In alignment with BSOM’s mission to increase the supply of primary care physicians serving the state, improve the health and well-being of the region, and train physicians who will meet the health care needs of the state, BSOM is committed to graduating physicians who are prepared to meet the highest standards of clinical care and who serve with integrity and compassion.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
Typically students fulfill the MBA requirements between their third and fourth years of medical studies, but requests for other time frames may be submitted. Interested students should schedule an appointment with the Associate Dean of Student Affairs at Brody School of Medicine to discuss their eligibility and program requirements. Requests for approval should be submitted to the Office of Student Affairs by April 15 of the year in which a student intends to enter the MD/MBA Program. The MD/MBA Admissions Committee will determine each student’s eligibility and notify them of their decision. 

Students enrolled in the Dual MD/MPH option can take MPH coursework during summer vacations, a leave of absence between the third and fourth year of medical school, and distance education.
MPH degree requirements for medical students are identical to the requirements of other MPH students. Medical students should be able to complete requirements for both degrees in five years.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
The Medical College Admission Test (MCAT) is required of all applicants. Applicants are asked to take this test in the spring, but no later than the summer, of the year prior to their desired matriculation date to medical school.

All successful applicants will have completed an undergraduate degree before enrollment. Each applicant must have the equivalent of at least three years of acceptable work at an accredited college or university prior to applying to our school. No specific undergraduate major is required, but regardless of the major interest area, the applicant must have completed all prerequisite coursework prior to gaining admission. We recommend core science courseowork be completed prior to taking the MCAT. AP credit courses and online courses are not accepted to meet prerequisite requirements.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Within five years of degree completion, not 5 years from when the course was taken.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: All available application data are evaluated: MCAT scores; academic performance; comments contained in letters of reference/recommendation; clinical/service/research/leadership experiences; and (for invited applicants) the results of two personal interviews, conducted by two members of the Admissions Committee.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: We encourage shadowing as an introduction to the clinical environment. We also strongly encourage applicants to obtain hands-on clinical care experience prior to applying (e.g., CNA, EMT, medical assistant, scribe). While clinical experiences across specialties are valuable, clinical hours completed in primary care settings are particularly emphasized in our review process.
